verdict.rationale: React's own docs say you can add React to an existing HTML page and render interactive components anywhere on it without rewriting the project. The createRoot reference adds that a page with 'sprinkles' of React can have as many separate roots as needed, with identifierPrefix to avoid ID conflicts between roots. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of dropping React into a server-rendered page, and documented detail on the minimal setup steps (e.g., whether a build tool is required) for a non-React page.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drop the framework into an existing server-rendered HTML page and render interactive components without rewriting the whole page

citations.quote: You don’t have to build your whole page in React. Add React to your existing HTML page, and render interactive React components anywhere on it.
If you want to add some interactivity to your existing project, you don't have to rewrite it in React. Add React to your existing stack, and render interactive React components anywhere.
A page that uses "sprinkles" of React for parts of the page may have as many separate roots as needed.
createRoot lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node.
Useful to avoid conflicts when using multiple roots on the same page.
